title: Profile-Based Auditing of Domestic Violence Survey Selection Across South Asia
abstract: arXiv:2611.15106v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Domestic violence (DV) data in the Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) are collected through a specialized module whose household-level sampling and privacy requirements create a distinct observation process. We ask whether demographic, socioeconomic, and household characteristics form reproducible population profiles and whether these profiles contain information about selection into the DV module across South Asia. Using DHS Individual Recode data for 796,374 women aged 15-49 across Afghanistan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, and Pakistan, we harmonize 61 numeric and 8 categorical features, reduce the profile space with PCA, and identify six interpretable profiles. translated_title: 基于画像的南亚家庭暴力调查选择审计
translated_abstract: 人口与健康调查（DHS）中的家庭暴力（DV）数据通过专门模块收集，其住户层面的抽样和隐私要求形成了一种独特的观测过程。我们探究人口统计、社会经济和住户特征能否形成可重现的人群画像，以及这些画像是否包含关于南亚各地区家庭暴力模块选择信息。研究使用了覆盖阿富汗、印度、缅甸、尼泊尔和巴基斯坦的796,374名15-49岁女性的DHS个体重编码数据，统一协调了61个数值特征和8个分类特征，通过主成分分析（PCA）降低画像空间维度，并识别出六个可解释的画像。随后，在考虑初级抽样单元的留出验证框架下评估了22个机器学习模型。表现最佳的模型HistGradientBoosting达到了ROC-AUC 0.9167和PR-AUC 0.9612，而仅基于抽样设计的基线分别为0.8475和0.9203。加入女性个体层面的特征可进一步……
tldr: 本研究利用机器学习模型对南亚五国近80万女性的特征画像进行分析，发现人口与社会经济特征能够高度预测家庭暴力调查模块的样本选择，从而为审计DHS家暴数据的选择偏差和代表性提供了画像审计方法。
en_tdlr: This study uses machine learning on profiles of 796,374 women across five South Asian countries to show that demographic and socioeconomic characteristics strongly predict selection into the DHS domestic violence module, enabling profile-based auditing of survey selection bias.
